newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST - Irish Permanent profits seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Irish Permanent profits seen up.

text.p: A booming Irish housing market is expected to boost profits of financial services group Irish Permanent Plc by up to 13 percent when it reports results for 1996 on Tuesday.
"If they do not do well in this market they will never do well," one analyst said.
Irish Permanent, a building society which floated on the stock exchange in October 1994, has 80 percent of its loan book in residential mortgages.

With Ireland's house prices up 15 percent year-on-year to September 1996, and mortgage lending up 16.8 percent year-on-year to December 1996, Irish Permanent is expected to be a major beneficiary of Ireland's economic success.
"I am expect earning per share (EPS) growth of about 12 percent," Riada stockbrokers analyst Eamon Hughes said.
Hughes is forecasting EPS at 32.4 pence per share versus 28.9 pence per share in 1995 and pre-tax profit at 47.5 million punts versus 42.4 million punts in 1995.
Goodbody stockbrokers analyst Oliver O'Shea sees a pre-tax profit of 48 million and EPS of 32.6 pence per share.
"I would think they (Irish Permanent) are holding their own in the market although the main banks are taking more of the business than they traditionally have done," O'Shea said.
Some analysts believe Irish Permanent's share price at 590 Irish pence is overvalued, bloated by takeover speculation.
"The share price is not reflecting what Irish Permanent is doing in the market. It is more reflecting a takeout bid by Abbey National," O'Shea said.
Britain's Abbey National took a 9.9 percent stake in Irish Permanent when Ireland's leading building society converted to plc status.
Abbey National said at the time that it intended to maintain a long-term minority investment in Irish Permanent.

The British financial services group is restrained from increasing its shareholding under the Building Societies Act, 1989, which states no person or group can own more than 15 percent of the issued share capital of Irish Permanent Plc for a period of five years after conversion.
Market sources believe Abbey National will bid outright for the company once the five years are up.

"It is on the cards that Abbey National will take out Irish Permanent, probably late in 1999," O'Shea said. "It is basically a similar business to Abbey National's and has a good market share so it will be a good fit."
